children: November 24 (Renewables Now) - Green Volt, a floating wind project off the east coast of Scotland, has signed an agreement with turbine maker Siemens Gamesa to reserve manufacturing capacity and specialist engineering resources for 28 turbines of more than 15 MW each.

The multimillion-pound deal, unveiled today, marks a key step forward for the project, which is being developed by Flotation Energy and Vargronn around 50 miles off Peterhead. Green Volt has consent for up to 560 MW of capacity and holds a 400-MW contract for difference (CfD) from the UK government, secured in 2024.

In addition, Green Volt has signed a letter of intent with the Port of Aberdeen for anchor and mooring marshalling activities at Aberdeen South Harbour. The arrangement is set to support GBP 15 million (USD 19.4m/EUR 17.7m) in investment and spending on port infrastructure, facilities and supply chain activities.
"These are landmark agreements for Green Volt and a defining moment for floating offshore wind. Reserving turbines of this scale is a world first,” said Green Volt Project Director Matt Green.

“Alongside our agreement with the Port of Aberdeen, it represents significant progress towards construction, building momentum for further major contracts and investment as we move towards delivering floating wind at commercial scale,” Green added.

“While it still has important milestones ahead, reserving manufacturing capacity for 28 of our 15-MW turbines is a meaningful step in moving the project forward,” said Darren Davidson, Managing Director of Siemens Energy UK & Ireland.

Commenting on the announcement, RenewableUK’s CEO Tara Singh said: "Aberdeen is a critical hub for the future of the energy transition and today's announcement will boost the development of our floating wind supply chain in the north east of Scotland and nationwide, including turbine manufacturing in Hull. The infrastructure, engineering and capabilities being developed for Green Volt will benefit future commercial-scale floating wind projects all around the UK."

title: Green Volt reserves capacity for Siemens Gamesa turbines
